_doc: Risk tiers for the Merge gate check and for land_pr.py. The tier is set by the change, not by who wrote it.

dan: waits for Dan. The Merge gate check fails until the repository owner adds the approved_label after the latest commit. Once added, label (needs-dan) still counts after someone removes it. low: only prose and images. normal: everything else. The gate passes low and normal; land_pr.py also wants an independent review line for normal.

dan.relief lets three stop-list changes through without Dan, since none can change what runs: reference (a file byte-identical to the same path in the reference repo at ref), comment_only (files with these suffixes where only whole-line comments or blank lines outside block scalars changed) and back_merge (a PR into nightly whose every changed file already matches main or weekly, and that nightly hadn't changed since they last shared history). Remove a key to switch its rule off. A needs-dan label still holds.

dan.relief.plain_workflow frees a workflow from the stop list when its text, before, after and on the base's tip, holds no secret but GITHUB_TOKEN, no write access, no pull_request_target or workflow_run, no self-hosted runner, and the edit adds no continue-on-error, || true or if: false. It stays normal tier, so a reviewer still reads it. held_names and a repo's own dan patterns stay held. So every other workflow, including one with a new name, waits for Dan.

dan.except frees fastlane's store text and screenshots from the shared stop list, and low.except keeps the text at normal tier: a release takes it as reviewed. Nothing else under fastlane is freed, so review_information, tests and new files wait for Dan.
Globs: ** crosses folders, * and ? stay inside one folder, and case doesn't count. A rename is judged by both its old and new path.

Per repo: dan adds stop-list paths; low_heads names automation branches whose workflow-opened PRs are low; no_ci_ok lets land_pr.py land a PR when the repo's path-filtered CI doesn't run for it; own_gate leaves stop-list PRs to the repo's own merge job.
Everything in this repository is on its own stop list, so a PR can't loosen the rules that judge it.

dfakkeldy/merge-gate.note: This repository is the gate. Every repo runs its main branch, so any change here (even a new file beside merge_gate.py) changes the rule everywhere.
